description: UNIQUE enforcement is opt-in via the engine's constraints.enforce.uniqueKey property and OFF by default, so on a default engine a UNIQUE column is informational only - exactly as on Snowflake - and a duplicate non-null value inserts without complaint. The enforcement-ON behaviour (rejecting a duplicate across statements and within one multi-row INSERT, accepting distinct values, and leaving NULLs unconstrained) needs an engine built with that property set, which has no SQL surface, and stays in features/UniqueKeyEnforcementTest. Converted from that class, which is trimmed to its four enforcement-ON tests.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, email VARCHAR UNIQUE)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM t
